Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for India's reply. It is still quite overcast as the two umpires make their way out to the middle followed by Hugh Weibgen and the rest of the Aussies. It will be the left-hand right-hand combination of Adarsh Singh and Arshin Kulkarni to open the innings for India Under-19. Callum Vidler will kick things off with the new ball for Australia Under-19. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, Australia have the runs on the board and have their noses in front at the halfway mark. They have gone in with four pacers who will look to exploit the conditions. As for India, it will require a record chase if they are to clinch the title for the sixth time. They have the batting firepower to get over the line, and it will all come down to how they fare against the new ball. A mouth-watering chase awaits us. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Harjas Singh is down for a chat. He says that it was good to start off steadily and take his time and when the bad balls came, he was able to put them away. Adds that spin is his strong point and a prior tour to Sri Lanka helped his batting. Reckons that the score is a big one and hopefully, they can defend it.

On the other hand, India Under-19 will be a bit disappointed that they allowed Australia to get past 250 and now have a challenging total to overhaul. What looked to be a good toss to lose at the start, India were relying on their pacers to make the overcast conditions count. As he has done in this competition, Raj Limbani helped India draw the first blood. It was followed by a quiet middle phase for India, which was dominated by the gritty stand between Hugh Weibgen and Harry Dixon. Uday Saharan turned to one of his wicket-taking options in Naman Tiwari, and the left-arm seamer helped them claw their way back into the game with a double strike. Harjas Singh took the attack to them, but he was nipped in the bud by Saumy Pandey. After that, India kept chipping away with wickets and did not allow Australia to run away with the game. Raj Limbani was the pick of the bowlers for India with figures of 3 for 38 from his 10 overs.

Ollie Peake finishes with a flourish to help Australia Under-19 breach the 250-run mark! The Aussies end up with 253 on the board, the highest-ever total in the history of the Men's Under-19 World Cup final. After the skipper, Hugh Weibgen called it right and opted to put runs on the board, they were dealt an early setback with Sam Konstas departing for a duck. Coming in at number 3, Hugh Weibgen joined hands with Harry Dixon to see off that phase with the new ball. The two batters played low-risk cricket, with Weibgen dominating the partnership. However, Weibgen fell on 48, and Dixon was dismissed soon after, which put the Aussies on the back foot. Harjas Singh and Ryan Hicks then got together to rebuild the inning for their team. Harjas delivered when it mattered the most and snapped his form slump with a fighting fifty. After Harjas's departure, Olivier Peake kept the scoreboard ticking and found good support from the tail. Peake remained unbeaten on 46 and got Australia the finish they were after.

FOUR! Ollie Peake finishes with a flourish and takes Australia Under-19 over the 250-run mark. Full and outside off, Peake hangs deep in the crease and reaches out before powering it through wide mid off for a boundary to end the first innings of the Final. Australia Under-19 finish with 253/7, the highest total in an Under-19 World Cup Final.

Callum Vidler is down for a chat. He says that they had a little celebration after the semi-final, then had a day off and then back to training and are ready for the game. Adds that the only thing that matters is that they bowl out the opposition and win and aren't bothered about personal milestones. On the rivalry between Australia and India, he says that he isn't that familiar with the rivalry itself and wants to do what the men did a few months ago.

Arshin Kulkarni is in for a chat. He says that he was thinking about the game last night but had a good sleep. Reckons that it is more about the mental side of the game than the technique on these wickets. Says that Australia Under-19 have good bowers, but he is ready to attack and defend. On the overhead conditions, he replies that it is very different from the last one and a half months and that it is much cooler, which should help the pacers. Ends by saying that the BCCI secretary wished all the boys in the meeting and that there has been plenty of support from India.

PITCH REPORT - HD Ackerman is pitchside and reckons that the decision to bat first is an interesting one as the conditions are overcast and it is pretty humid as well. Adds that on one side it is 64 meters and 63 meters on the other side and the straight boundary is 82 meters. Abhinav Mukund joins him and says that the theme in Benoni has been the bounce and that there could be variable bounce later on as there are cracks and it hasn't been watered either.

The skipper of India Under-19, Uday Saharan says that they were prepared to do both but would have batted first had they won the toss. Informs that they are going with an unchanged team. Mentions that they are allowed to play only one Under-19 World Cup and therefore, it would mean a lot for the boys to lift the trophy. States that they will look to the game deep and keep in wickets in hand.

The captain of Australia Under-19, Hugh Weibgen says they will bat first. Says that it is a bit overcast but they are happy to bat first and runs on the board matter. Adds that they didn't get much sleep after the semi-final win but had a good training session yesterday and are ready to go. Mentions that they want to replicate what the senior men's team has done in the last 12 months or so. Informs that they have one change with Charlie Anderson coming in for Tom Campbell.

The grand finale of the 2024 Under-19 World Cup is poised to unfold, pitting two perennial rivals, India and Australia, against each other at Willowmoore Park in Benoni. In the blue corner, we have India, the defending champions and record holders, with an impressive tally of five Men's Under-19 World Cup titles. Standing tall in the yellow corner is Australia, boasting three previous triumphs. The stage is set for a clash of titans reminiscent of their encounter in the final of the 2023 Men's ODI World Cup, where the Aussies emerged victorious, breaking Indian hearts in the process. Hugh Weibgen's boys will aim to draw inspiration from that famous win, while Uday Saharan and his determined squad take to the field with a burning desire to avenge the agonizing defeat suffered by their senior counterparts. The reigning champions, India, faced their toughest test yet in the semi-final against the hosts, South Africa. In pursuit of 245 runs for a place in the final, India struggled against the lethal Proteas pairing of Kwena Maphaka and Tristan Luus, finding themselves at 32-4. Captain Uday Saharan and Sachin Dhas then combined forces, crafting a remarkable 171-run partnership that rescued the Indian team from a dire situation. Uday Saharan, Musheer Khan, and Sachin Dhas are the top three run-getters in the competition, highlighting the consistent performance of the batting unit, which has eased the pressure on the bowlers. Skipper Saharan has played the role of the anchor throughout the tournament, with other batters rallying around him. The opening duo, Arshin Kulkarni and Adarsh Singh face the onus of providing a solid start after experiencing a dip in form in the last few games. On the bowling front, vice-captain Saumy Pandey has been instrumental with his left-arm spin, leading the wicket-taking charts for India. The pace duo of Raj Limbani and Naman Tiwari has effectively utilised the new ball, while Murugan Abhishek and Musheer Khan have maintained control over runs in the middle phase. As for Australia, in the semi-final against Pakistan, Tom Straker's six-wicket haul played a pivotal role in restricting the Asian side to 179. Australia were in control for most parts of the chase until they began to crumble under pressure. Thanks to the 17-run last-wicket stand between Callum Vidler and Rafael Macmillan, the Aussies edged out Pakistan in a low-scoring thriller. That said, Peake scored a crucial 49 in the semi-final, while Tom Campbell also chipped in, which is a positive sign for the boys in canary yellow. As far as their pace department is concerned, Callum Vidler and Tom Straker have done the bulk of the damage, and the pair have been well-complemented by Mahli Beardman. When it comes to spin bowling duties, Rafael Macmillan and Tom Campbell have been the ones to watch out for.
